title: Choosing the motor, power supply, and Jrk
creator: Pololu
why: Connects motor loading to controller and supply requirements.
first_task: Separate stall current, free-running current, and continuous driver limits on a candidate's specification card.
limitations: Written around a particular controller family; verify the actual driver and motor datasheets.
evidence_note: Opened manufacturer guide; voltage/current ratings, stall behavior, and supply selection sections are available.

title: Speed–Torque Curves for Stepper Motors
creator: Oriental Motor
why: Shows why a curve belongs to a motor-and-driver combination.
first_task: Read three points and record the voltage, driver, and test conditions beside them.
limitations: Example curves do not rate a different motor, supply, or driver.
evidence_note: Opened official article; holding torque, pullout boundary, and curve-generation conditions are described.

title: How to Improve Motion Smoothness and Accuracy of Stepper Motors
creator: Dipankar Mitra, Texas Instruments
why: Distinguishes command subdivision from load-dependent motion accuracy.
first_task: Explain why a smaller command can fail to overcome friction without claiming the motor loses all holding torque.
limitations: Driver examples and measurements are specific; they do not establish accuracy for your mechanism.
evidence_note: Opened revision A; incremental-torque discussion and current-sense/driver effects are present.

title: DYNAMIXEL XM430-W210 e-Manual
creator: ROBOTIS
prerequisites: Position, velocity, current, and torque distinctions.
why: Provides a concrete example of an integrated actuator's modes and limits.
first_task: Locate current, position, temperature, and shutdown information; distinguish stall torque from continuous operation.
limitations: A study reference, not a selected part for this guide; mode and protocol behavior are model-specific.
evidence_note: Opened official manual; operating modes, control table, and stall-versus-performance warning are available.

title: Quasi-Direct Drive for Low-Cost Compliant Robotic Manipulation
creator: David V. Gealy and collaborators, University of California, Berkeley
prerequisites: Motor sizing, reflected inertia, and feedback basics.
why: Connects transmission choice to a complete robot's mechanical and thermal compromises.
first_task: Trace why the authors move motor mass with belts, then list which assumptions differ for our arm.
limitations: Results describe Blue; its performance and safety do not transfer to a new printed design.
evidence_note: Opened abstract and eight-page PDF; QDD design, belt packaging, experiments, and thermal discussion are present.

title: Light Power and Precision Drive Design Manual
creator: Gates
prerequisites: Torque, power, ratios, and unit conversion.
why: Shows the selection work that pitch circles and a ratio alone leave unfinished.
first_task: Find the effective-pull equation and explain why tight-side plus slack-side tension differs from their difference.
limitations: Ratings apply to specified belt systems; do not transfer them to an unknown belt or printed tooth profile.
evidence_note: Opened 112-page manual; selection tables and synchronous-belt effective/total tension formulas are present.

title: Principle of HarmonicDrive
creator: Harmonic Drive Systems
why: Makes the moving tooth-engagement regions visible.
first_task: Follow one wave-generator turn and calculate the signed ratio for 200 and 202 teeth.
limitations: Explains a principle; it does not provide a printable tooth design or fatigue rating.
evidence_note: Opened official operating-principle page; three components and two-tooth relative advance are described.

title: Cycloidal Gear Technology and RV Mechanism
creator: Nabtesco Motion Control
prerequisites: Gear ratios and bearing load paths.
why: Links the cycloidal motion to paired discs and support bearings in a commercial architecture.
first_task: Identify the fast input, eccentric motion, slow output, and bearings carrying external loads.
limitations: Product performance claims are specific to Nabtesco's construction, not generic or printed cycloidal drives.
evidence_note: Opened official explanation; two-stage RV mechanism, eccentric crankshafts, paired gears, and integrated bearings are described.

title: Voice Coil Actuators vs. Solenoids
creator: H2W Technologies
prerequisites: Force, travel, current, and duty cycle.
why: Compares two actuators that can look similar but behave differently across travel.
first_task: Write why a seated solenoid force does not establish its starting force.
limitations: A broad comparison; specialized proportional and latching solenoids require their own specifications.
evidence_note: Opened official article; stroke, direction, current/force, and positioning differences are described.

title: Series Elastic Actuators
creator: Matthew M. Williamson, MIT
prerequisites: Springs, dynamics, and basic feedback control.
access: Free repository report; copyrighted, link rather than redistribute.
why: Develops intentional series compliance as a force-control design choice.
first_task: Explain what the spring sensor measures and why softer mechanics change achievable response.
limitations: Research-era hardware and experiments; use the reasoning without transferring ratings to our study.
evidence_note: Opened MIT repository record and report PDF; design, theoretical performance, and measured evaluation are present.

title: Flexinol Actuator Wire Technical and Design Data
creator: Dynalloy
prerequisites: Force, strain, resistance, and heat flow.
why: Makes wire diameter, load, and cooling conditions explicit.
first_task: Compare cooling-time conditions before estimating a repeat cycle.
limitations: Guidelines are condition-specific; this guide does not supply a powered-wire build procedure.
evidence_note: Opened data table and notes, including the 0.10 mm wire row and static-air cooling conditions.

title: Piezo Actuator Displacement Behavior
creator: Physik Instrumente
why: Explains why fine command resolution does not eliminate path-dependent displacement.
first_task: Sketch two paths to the same voltage and explain why displacement can differ.
limitations: Material behavior is not a driver or complete stage specification; consult the linked force and dynamics topics too.
evidence_note: Opened official tutorial; nonlinearity, hysteresis, creep, and position-control sections are available.
